novelty.justification: The claim proposes a new phenomenon/mechanism, specifically that “more fragmented numerals cause a model to think longer on the exact same problem, inflating tokens without improving accuracy,” mediated by a “prompt-boundary residual stream” budget signal. The closest retrieved work is “Tokenization Constraints in LLMs: A Study of Symbolic and Arithmetic Reasoning Limits,” which links numeral tokenization to arithmetic and symbolic-reasoning performance, while “Do NOT Think That Much for 2+3=? On the Overthinking of o1-Like LLMs” studies excess reasoning compute; searches using “numeral tokenization reasoning length,” “token fragmentation overthinking,” “tokenization compute tax reasoning models,” “prompt boundary length predictor reasoning,” and “tokenization-induced overthinking” did not identify an essentially equivalent study. The step from those works to this claim requires a new core relationship—surface numeral fragmentation causing matched-accuracy inference-time compute inflation and a causal budget representation—rather than a direct transfer or mere object substitution, supporting high but within-framework novelty.
